bug_semantics: A crafted NFS server can advertise an ONC-RPC record-marker length smaller than the READ payload length encoded in the response. In rpc_read_from_socket's READ_IOVEC state, libnfs used the decoded/expected READ size as pdu_size and subtracted it from the unsigned record bytes remaining in rm_xid[0] without first proving pdu_size <= rm_xid[0]. When the expected PDU size exceeds the absolute record-marker size, that subtraction wraps the remaining-length counter, so the stream parser can treat a malformed record as having a huge residual/padding length and consume data outside the declared record.
flaw_origin: The zero-copy READ3 implementation introduced READ_IOVEC and began tracking two independently attacker-influenced sizes—the decoded READ count and the record-marker remainder—without enforcing their ordering before subtraction. The earliest reconstructable source commit is topic-branch commit b555b6ed4efca6e10b1e2e16c0b44e25a5c5d1bd; its vulnerable hunk was later replayed as part of the larger main-line zero-copy integration 5e8f7ce273308eb77f94248f4501e574a703c1a5 and subsequently mechanically changed from local pdu_size to rpc->pdu_size by 84ebfa53b6811a7da68a9342ce13537b91653490.
ai_marker: absent — the exact BIC commit object names human author Ronnie Sahlberg <ronniesahlberg@gmail.com> and human committer Ronnie Sahlberg <ronniesahlberg@gmail.com>; its only trailer is "Signed-off-by: Ronnie Sahlberg <ronniesahlberg@gmail.com>" and it has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool, or bot marker.
evidence: Advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-27p2-fpv6-cj8c identifies CVE-2026-57918/CWE-191 in READ_IOVEC in lib/socket.c, triggered when expected PDU size exceeds the xid/record-marker size, and points to 935b8db712b3c6649bc57ddc276526c4a31680de.

First-party fix: https://github.com/sahlberg/libnfs/commit/935b8db712b3c6649bc57ddc276526c4a31680de (parent 1efd760b692623146ce681e18d78a9c939de079e) adds exactly `if (rpc->rm_xid[0] < rpc->pdu_size) return -1;` before `rpc->rm_xid[0] -= rpc->pdu_size` in lib/socket.c, directly preventing the unsigned underflow.

History search `git log --all --reverse -S'rpc->rm_xid[0] -= pdu_size' -- lib/socket.c` found the original topic implementation b555b6ed4efca6e10b1e2e16c0b44e25a5c5d1bd, later branch replays, main integration 5e8f7ce273308eb77f94248f4501e574a703c1a5, and the later member-field refactor 84ebfa53b6811a7da68a9342ce13537b91653490. The original public commit is https://github.com/sahlberg/libnfs/commit/b555b6ed4efca6e10b1e2e16c0b44e25a5c5d1bd.

BIC diff b555b6ed4efca6e10b1e2e16c0b44e25a5c5d1bd adds READ_IOVEC and the unchecked subtraction at lib/socket.c:615-618; reviewer line view: https://github.com/sahlberg/libnfs/blob/b555b6ed4efca6e10b1e2e16c0b44e25a5c5d1bd/lib/socket.c#L615-L618.

Direct-parent verification: `git grep -n -E 'READ_IOVEC|rm_xid\[0\] -= .*pdu_size' da3d38031c8027c78d8f336e746a6d88435daf4c -- lib/socket.c` returned no match, while the same command on b555b6ed4efca6e10b1e2e16c0b44e25a5c5d1bd returned READ_IOVEC at lines 499/603/615 and the vulnerable subtraction at line 618. Thus the vulnerable mechanism is absent from the BIC's immediate parent tree.

The affected main-line replay is https://github.com/sahlberg/libnfs/commit/5e8f7ce273308eb77f94248f4501e574a703c1a5 (30-file zero-copy/API aggregate). Its lib/socket.c:634-638 contains the same READ_IOVEC subtraction hunk. Commit 84ebfa53b6811a7da68a9342ce13537b91653490 only replaces local `pdu_size` with the rpc_context member and is therefore a refactor, not the semantic BIC.

Release-boundary checks: tag libnfs-5.0.3 resolves to 4379837536d9eac537810dc7b13071136049b22a and has neither the vulnerable member-form subtraction nor main integration 5e8f7ce273308eb77f94248f4501e574a703c1a5 as an ancestor. libnfs-6.0.0 (976a9ae7dc3d7fcbd10cd2db4cd65d4a2c092030), 6.0.1, and 6.0.2 (18c5c73ee88bb7dc8da0d55dc95164bb77e49dc6) contain 5e8f7ce273308eb77f94248f4501e574a703c1a5 and the unchecked line; this establishes 6.0.0-6.0.2 as the affected tagged releases, consistent with the advisory's 'through 6.0.2' description.

Fixed-boundary checks: 935b8db712b3c6649bc57ddc276526c4a31680de is not an ancestor of libnfs-6.0.2 but is an ancestor of libnfs-7.0.0. Tag libnfs-7.0.0 resolves to 8563deedbedcbf88130460de4d01fbf68dad58ad and contains the new bounds check immediately before the subtraction, making 7.0.0 the first fixed tagged release.
reasoning: The advisory and its sole first-party source reference identify a size underflow in READ_IOVEC and a three-line direct fix. Tracing the vulnerable subtraction semantically, rather than accepting current blame, shows that b555b6ed4efca6e10b1e2e16c0b44e25a5c5d1bd first created the zero-copy READ_IOVEC path and unchecked record-remainder subtraction; its immediate parent da3d38031c8027c78d8f336e746a6d88435daf4c has neither READ_IOVEC nor the subtraction. The larger main-line integration 5e8f7ce273308eb77f94248f4501e574a703c1a5 replays that hunk and is what carries it into releases 6.0.0 through 6.0.2, while 84ebfa53b6811a7da68a9342ce13537b91653490 merely moves pdu_size into rpc_context and cannot be the BIC. Fix 935b8db712b3c6649bc57ddc276526c4a31680de enforces the missing size invariant and is included in 7.0.0. Finally, attribution is based only on the exact b555b6ed4efca6e10b1e2e16c0b44e25a5c5d1bd commit object: it has human author/committer identity and no AI marker, so the closed causal verdict is NOT_AI.
